description: Egyptian Arabic (Cairene colloquial, Arabic script) core building blocks for B1 learners: existence, have, negation, modals, present and future.

terms.definition: Says something exists: there is, there are. With a question tone, it asks if something is around.
terms.example: فيه صيدلية قريبة من هنا؟ — Is there a pharmacy near here?
terms.discussion: The negative is one word, مفيش: مفيش عيش, there's no bread. You'll hear it all day.

terms.definition: Wants something, or wants to do something. A noun or a present verb comes right after.
terms.example: أنا عايز اتنين شاي، لو سمحت. — Two teas, please.
terms.discussion: It agrees with the speaker like an adjective: a woman says عايزة, a group says عايزين.

terms.definition: Marks habits and actions happening now. Add بـ to the present verb: بشتغل, I work or I'm working.
terms.example: إنت بتشتغل فين دلوقتي؟ — Where are you working these days?
terms.anti_example: Not أنا أشرب قهوة كل يوم: without بـ it sounds unfinished. Say بشرب قهوة كل يوم.

terms.definition: Negates words that aren't verbs, like adjectives, nouns and عايز. The future with حـ takes it too.
terms.example: لا، شكرًا يا طنط، أنا مش جعان. — No thanks, auntie, I'm not hungry.
terms.anti_example: Not مش شربت for 'I didn't drink': a past verb takes ما…ش, so مشربتش.

terms.definition: Obligation: must, have to. It never changes, whoever you're talking about.
terms.example: لازم أمشي دلوقتي، الساعة اتناشر. — I have to go, it's midnight.
terms.anti_example: Not مش لازم for 'you mustn't': that means 'you don't have to'. For 'mustn't', say ماينفعش.

terms.definition: Your 'have' in Egyptian: عند plus an ending for the owner, as in عندي, عندك, عنده.
terms.example: عندك شاحن؟ الموبايل فصل. — Got a charger? My phone died.
terms.anti_example: Not مش عندي for 'I don't have': it takes ما…ش, so معنديش.

terms.definition: Politely asks for something, or says it's possible: can I, could you, maybe.
terms.example: ممكن الحساب، لو سمحت؟ — Can we have the bill, please?
terms.discussion: On its own it answers 'maybe': جاي بكرة؟ ممكن. Starting a request with it already sounds polite.

terms.definition: Wraps a verb to negate it: ما before, ش after, as in مفهمتش, I didn't understand.
terms.example: أنا مبحبش القهوة من غير سكر. — I don't like coffee without sugar.
terms.discussion: People usually write ما as just م stuck to the verb: مبحبش. The future still takes مش: مش حروح.

terms.definition: Talks about real ability: can, be able to. It changes with the person: أقدر, تقدر, يقدر.
terms.example: مقدرش آجي النهارده، أنا تعبان. — I can't come today, I'm sick.
terms.discussion: For asking a favour, Egyptians usually start with ممكن instead. يقدر is more about whether you really can.

terms.definition: Puts a verb in the future: add حـ to the present verb, as in حسافر, I'll travel.
terms.example: حنروح إسكندرية يوم الخميس. — We're going to Alexandria on Thursday.
terms.discussion: Many people write it هـ instead: هسافر. Read both spellings as the same thing.

relationships.description: مش negates words that are not conjugated verbs; ما…ش wraps the verb itself.
Don't have is معنديش: عند takes ما…ش, not مش.
